issue_context.title: Modbus Climate - Not possible to configure same address for hvac mode on multiple devices since 2024.1.0
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Since 2024.1.0 it is no longer possible to configure multiple climate devices with the same register for hvac mode.

I have a floor heating which I control via modbus. Before 2024.1.0 it was possible to have multiple climates devices configured which use the same address for controlling the hvac mode. In my example I'm only able to control the mode for the whole floor level and not for each room but the room temperature could be different.

It looks like this was coming with the following pull request #104577 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.1.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.12.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

modbus

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus/#address

### Diagnostics information

Logger: homeassistant.components.modbus.validators
Source: components/modbus/validators.py:291
Integration: Modbus (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 13:32:21 (4 occurrences)
Last logged: 13:32:21

Modbus climate/Fußbodenheizung Bad/Flur address 1_1 is duplicate, second entry not loaded!
Modbus climate/Fußbodenheizung Ankleidezimmer address 1_1 is duplicate, second entry not loaded!
Modbus climate/Fußbodenheizung Badezimmer address 1_1 is duplicate, second entry not loaded!
Modbus climate/Fußbodenheizung Schlafzimmer address 1_1 is duplicate, second entry not loaded!


### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
modbus:

# Heizkreise Erdgeschloss
  - name: hub1
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.178.153
    port: 502
    climates:
      - name: "Fußbodenheizung Wohnzimmer/Küche"  #Heizkreis 01 und 02
        unique_id: fh_wohnzimmer
        hvac_mode_register: 
          address: 1
          values:
            state_off: 0
            state_heat: 1
        slave: 1
        data_type: int16
        #count: 1
        scale: 0.1
        offset: 0
        precision: 1
        max_temp: 30
        min_temp: 15
        temp_step: 0.5
        target_temp_register: 51
        address: 50
        input_type: input
      - name: "Fußbodenheizung Bad/Flur"
        unique_id: fh_badflur
        hvac_mode_register: 
          address: 1
          values:
            state_off: 0
            state_heat: 1
        slave: 1
        data_type: int16
        #count: 1
        scale: 0.1
        offset: 0
        precision: 1
        max_temp: 30
        min_temp: 15
        temp_step: 0.5
        target_temp_register: 53
        address: 52
        input_type: input
```

Modbus climate/Fußbodenheizung Badezimmer address 1_1 is duplicate, second entry not loaded!

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/81458dbf6f5bbeac9299182067a7762cd02d2717/homeassistant/components/modbus/validators.py#L274C1-L278C1


Is the part in the code which cause the problem

This is a design decision, one register belong to one entity, you will see that is a general design concept of most integrations.

Pull requests are welcome, but please do not forget, if this definition is removed, the pull request must ensure that all entities using the same register is updated when the register is read.

Before 2024.1 you surely could see that the different entities showed different values for a time after a change, until all entities have been updated with their scan intervals, that is a very wrong behavior.

Closing this, as it is not a bug.

review_comments:
One register in one device can only belong to one entity. Allowing one register to belong to multiple entities, would cause a lot of update problems !

Apart from that please explain why one register need to be allowed from multiple entities, it is not logical !

Your fix, only removes the check, but you miss the more important part to update all entities using this register. 

Currently we read one entity at the time, and update it....but you want to turn that around to when reading a register update n entities.

I already described that in the linked issue. The situation is that with 2023.12 and before this was possible. I had a floor heating which only have one mode register for all rooms. So in the past I changed it on one climate card and the others cards got updated with the next update from modbus. This was fine for me. Every card allows changing the overall mode.

With 2024.1.0 the mentioned code changes were added which makes this not possible anymore.

That might be, but you still need to address the issue of updating multiple entities when receiving a register value, and that is a major change of the update methods.

Apart from that I personally still feel it is wrong to use one register in multiple entities, but this is open source so my only concern is to secure your patch works correctly.
